description: Recipe for tools/import_real_track.py: Snetterton (Norfolk, UK), MSV. The 300 circuit with the 200 and 100 circuits sharing its base: all three current layouts (MSV's circuit-layouts page lists exactly these three; Wikipedia and racingcircuits.info give the same three, 2011 to date).
name: Snetterton
trackDescription: Snetterton, 300 (4.78 km), 200 (3.22 km) and 100 (1.58 km) circuits from OpenStreetMap, with heights, camber and terrain from the Environment Agency LIDAR Composite DTM (1 m). A flat former wartime airfield in open Norfolk farmland.
layoutSource: MSV official map 'Snetterton 300 Circuit' (snetterton.co.uk/about/circuit-layouts, 'SN Map_300 Circuit'): Senna Straight - Riches - Wilson - Palmer - Agostini - Hamilton - Oggies - Williams - Bentley Straight - Brundle - Nelson - Bomb Hole - Coram - Murrays; 2.969 mi / 4.779 km (Wikipedia, racingcircuits.info; MSV '3 miles').
directionSource: MSV official 300 map: the arrow beside the chequered flag on Senna Straight points west towards Riches (clockwise); driver61.com Snetterton 300 guide: turn 1 Riches, turn 2 Montreal (now Wilson), turn 3 Palmer ... turn 12 Murrays.

startFinish.note: OSM node 'Start/finish line' (raceway=start-finish) on Senna Straight, 459 m from Murrays.

startFinishSource: MSV official 300, 200 and 100 maps: the chequered flag on Senna Straight in front of the timekeeper's centre and race control, a little past half way from Murrays to Riches; OSM node 1717542072 'Start/finish line' 459 m along Senna Straight; BARC briefing notes: 'start line and finish line is located on the Senna Straight', 'in front of Race Control'; driver61.com gives the line at 52 27'48.2"N 0 56'41.0"E.

altLayouts.layoutSource: MSV official map 'Snetterton 200 Circuit': Riches and Wilson, then right at Chapman (OSM way 161975517) straight onto Bentley Straight, missing the infield (Palmer to Williams); 2.000 mi / 3.219 km (Wikipedia, racingcircuits.info; MSV '2 miles').
altLayouts.directionSource: MSV official 200 map: the same arrow by the flag on Senna Straight towards Riches (clockwise).
altLayouts.startFinishSource: MSV official 200 map: the chequered flag at the same place on Senna Straight as on the 300 map, so the 200 shares its line and grid.

altLayouts.layoutSource: MSV official map 'Snetterton 100 Circuit': the infield loop alone, Palmer - Agostini - Hamilton - Oggies, then Firmans (OSM way 161975518, mapped the other way) from the foot of Williams back onto the road to Palmer; 0.980 mi / 1.577 km (Wikipedia, racingcircuits.info; MSV '1 mile'). racingcircuits.info: the 200 'can be run simultaneously with the short 100 loop'.
altLayouts.directionSource: MSV official 100 map: the loop is the 300's infield driven the same way (Palmer, Agostini, Hamilton, Oggies, as the 300 map's arrow and driver61's turn order give them), joined by Firmans; as a loop on its own that is anticlockwise.

startFinish.note: ESTIMATED: on the straight from Palmer to Agostini beside the Tyrrells restaurant, 112 m after Palmer.

altLayouts.startFinishSource: ESTIMATED, no official source found: the MSV 100 map shows only the Senna Straight flag (grey, off the 100 loop) and no other line, and racingcircuits.info, Wikipedia and the BARC / MSV briefing notes found don't place one. The 100 runs while the 200 uses Senna Straight, so it can't share that line; the line is put on the infield's only long straight (Palmer to Agostini, beside the Tyrrells restaurant and the paddock), 112 m after Palmer, where the 24-car grid fits on the level. Chris to confirm.

widthNote: Not published; about 11-14 m on imagery (wide former airfield roads). One value for the whole lap.
expectedCornerOrderNote: Clockwise 300 lap as on the MSV map and in the driver61.com guide (Wilson was Montreal until 2021; OSM still has Montreal, relabelled here). Chapman (the 200's link) and Firmans (the 100's) aren't on the 300 lap, so they aren't labelled.

kerbs.source: driver61.com Snetterton 300 guide: 'I wouldn't advise using any of the kerbs' at the apexes (steep, old school); the outside exit kerb marks the edge of the usable road
driver61.com: a red sausage kerb on the inside before the apex; a triangle of exit kerb on the left
driver61.com: run the kerb from 1/4 to 3/4 of the way along; run the exit kerb but not beyond it
driver61.com: the apex kerb is usable; the exit kerb is plenty visible
driver61.com: the inside kerb with a large block; use all of the kerbing on the outside
driver61.com: use all of the apex kerb; grass-crete on the inside, worn grass at the exit
driver61.com: all of the inside kerb (careful with the tyre block); all of the exit kerbing
driver61.com: kerbing on the inside, run-off on the outside
driver61.com: all of the inside kerb (stay off the sausage kerb); all of the exit kerbing
driver61.com: the apex half way along the kerbing, all usable; a little of the exit kerbing
driver61.com: a small inside kerb that becomes a large, wide kerb after about 20 m
driver61.com: all of the inside kerb (not the sausage); all of the exit kerbing, a track-limits sensor beyond

kerbsNote: OSM has no kerb or run-off features at Snetterton (Overpass 2026-10-20: no barrier=kerb, kerb=* or area:highway), and the 1 m DTM can't resolve kerbs, so these overrides come from the driver61.com guide; Chapman and Firmans get the geometric placement.
